the synthesis of 5′-homo analogs of adenosine, AMP and ADP, which have been shown to be inhibitors of the enzyme 5′-AMP nucleosidase (EC 3.2.2.4) from E. coli.

the conformational analysis of the 5′-homonucleosides is not as simple as the analysis of their 3′-homo counterparts, but that the conformation of the 5'-homonucleoside is not necessarily different from that of the 3′-homolog.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5′-homo-AMP analog 4, the 5,6-dideoxy-6-phosphonomethyl derivative of the nucleoside 2, was synthesized and its structure was determined.
we have developed a new method for the preparation of 5′-homologs of adenosine and its nucleoside 5′-phosphates, and that these compounds have been characterized by NMR spectroscopy.
we have developed a novel and efficient synthetic method for the construction of the 5'-Homo-AMP-analogs, which is based on the use of 5'-homoadenosine derivatives as starting materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a 5′-homo modification in RNA can have a significant effect on the structure and dynamics of RNA, and that this modification is not a simple replacement of a ribo- with a deoxyribo-sugar.
we can now make a prediction of the 3D structure of a nucleic acid based on a 1D structure (sequence) alone, and this prediction is very accurate.
the presence of a 3’-phosphoryl group on the 5’-homo-AMP derivative 4 is sufficient for efficient binding to HIV reverse transcriptase.
